summary: TLS 0-RTT session-ticket replay by corporate firewall causes duplicate tokens and stream reordering for streaming responses (private deploy)
environment: prod (us-east-1, private deployment behind customer egress proxy)
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent duplication of tokens and out-of-order chunks in streaming chat responses when connected to our private deployment. The customer is on a private VPC deployment with an inline corporate TLS interception appliance (proxy/NGFW) that supports TLS 1.3 and performs session ticket handling.

Impact: Streams occasionally include duplicated token sequences or arrive partially reordered; client disconnects after retries. Customer engineering reports user-visible message duplication in production chat flows (~1-2% of streams during busy periods). This is P1 because it affects production UX for an enterprise tenant with private deployment.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed control plane peered over VPC), prod us-east-1, traffic egresses through customer inline TLS appliance that advertises support for TLS 1.3 0-RTT and performs session-ticket inspection/replay. Serving nodes run Redwood serving-runtime 2.8.1.

Observed symptoms:
- Streaming SSE/grpc streams open successfully, but payload sequence numbers indicate repeats (example log attached below).
- Reconnects happen mid-stream with TLS resumption; resumed sessions sometimes replay previously accepted 0-RTT data leading to duplicate application-layer tokens.
- End-to-end latency increases for affected streams as client attempts dedup and reconnect logic.

Initial hypothesis: The customer's middlebox is incorrectly re-sending (replaying) TLS 0-RTT session tickets or replaying early data across resumed sessions. Because 0-RTT data is not idempotent, replay at the TLS layer results in duplicate application payloads in the stream. Alternatively, the appliance may be incorrectly caching/forwarding session tickets across connections (e.g., between multiple client NAT endpoints) resulting in session resumption that causes the serving runtime to merge/accept early data twice.

Why different from normal control-plane TLS issues: This appears to be a middlebox-specific interaction with TLS 1.3 0-RTT semantics rather than an SNI/Host rewrite or presigned URL header problem. Standard networking checks (DNS, routing, host header) were not explanatory for the duplicated application payloads.

Immediate mitigations suggested to customer:
- Disable TLS 0-RTT/session-ticket resumption for egress to Redwood control plane and serving endpoints (configuration on the TLS appliance) as a temporary workaround.
- If appliance supports 0-RTT anti-replay or unique ticketing per client IP, enable strict anti-replay features.

Attachments: sample stream excerpt, server-side request IDs, client-side trace IDs (inline in logs below).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From customer private VPC with egress appliance enabled, start a streaming chat with a prompt that generates >1024 tokens.
2) Observe streaming chunks on client over time and track token sequence IDs (our SDK emits sequence_meta headers).
3) Trigger short TLS reconnects (simulate flapping egress path or brief NAT reuse) to encourage 0-RTT resumption from client side.
4) Inspect client/serving logs for repeated sequence IDs or duplicated token payloads.
logs: serving: req_id=svc-9a2f, stream_chunk_seq=128, payload_hash=abc123 (duplicate detected from same connection resumption path)
proxy: observed session_ticket issued_for=10.0.3.45, forwarded_to=10.0.3.46 (suspicious reuse)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-01 09:30 - Support: Confirmed customer is running an inline TLS appliance that performs man-in-the-middle TLS 1.3 and advertises 0-RTT support.

2026-03-01 10:15 - SRE: Reproduced duplicate-token behavior in lab by enabling 0-RTT resumption on test proxy and simulating quick reconnects; duplicates appear when the proxy replays early data across resumed sessions.

2026-03-02 14:40 - Eng (serving-runtime): Verified that serving-runtime accepts 0-RTT early data and applies it once per TLS connection; duplicate application-level events occur if early data is replayed by upstream appliance as a new connection (resumption).
2026-03-02 16:05 - Support: Confirmed customer appliance firmware is older and lacks proper anti-replay checks for session tickets when operating in multi-client mode behind NAT.
Related evidence: tcpdump and TLS debug show identical early_data payloads sent twice with different TCP connection 4-tuples after resumption.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-01: Customer first reported duplicated tokens in streaming session. Provided request IDs and client trace logs. Asked for immediate mitigation options.
Lars Becker (SRE) 2026-03-01: Performed lab repro with an appliance that replays 0-RTT early data. Confirmed duplication pattern. Recommending disabling 0-RTT as immediate workaround.
Customer (FinEdge) 2026-03-01: Confirmed they can temporarily disable 0-RTT on their appliance; requested guidance on config and whether Redwood can detect/reject duplicate early data.

Eve Dubois (Serving Eng) 2026-03-02: Noted that server-side dedup by application-level sequence IDs could be a fallback but has performance/complexity tradeoffs. Prefer appliance fix + short-term server-side conservative checks for identical early-data with identical sequence numbers during short window.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-03: Customer applied disable-0rtt config and reported reduction to ~0.01% duplication (within acceptable SLA), asked to keep ticket open while monitoring.
root_cause: Customer’s inline TLS appliance replays TLS 1.3 0-RTT (early_data) across resumed sessions due to session-ticket reuse across NATed clients and missing anti-replay protections. This causes non-idempotent application-level data to be processed twice by the serving runtime.
workaround: Advise customer to disable TLS 0-RTT/session-ticket resumption on the appliance for Redwood endpoints; enable anti-replay protections on appliance if available. Temporary server-side mitigations: add short-window de-duplication by sequence_meta and stronger session-identifier checks in the serving-runtime (engineering task).
resolution_plan: Short term: Customer to disable 0-RTT for Redwood endpoints (done 2026-03-02, customer reports improvement).

Mid term: Engineering to implement a low-overhead detection heuristic in serving-runtime to detect identical early_data with same sequence_meta arriving on resumed sessions within a short timeframe (RFC/design doc in progress).
Long term: Update private-deploy runbook to include guidance about TLS 1.3 0-RTT and recommended appliance settings; include a checklist for deployments behind NATed inline proxies.
